whyThisShow: This is a canonically legendary Wall of Sound-era Winterland show, officially released as part of 'Winterland 1973: The Complete Recordings.' The center of gravity is the second set, where one reviewer called the Dark Star > Eyes sequence "55 minutes of extremely well spent time" [source: 'the DS>eyes is 55 minutes of extremely well spent time']. The Dark Star itself draws repeated attention: one listener called it "a tour de force of psychedelic jazz" and dubbed it the "thinking man's Dark Star" [source: 'a tour de force of psychedelic jazz(after listening i understand why it has been dubbed the "thinking man's Dark Star"']. One voice notes the show is not without small flaws — there are recording dropouts in Eyes of the World and Half-Step patched with an audience source [source: 'dropouts during eyes and 1/2 step, but they are patched with an aud source i believe'] — and one reviewer rates the Dark Star not as the hottest version but as "really spacy and dreamy" [source: 'The Dark Star is not the hottest version, but really spacy and dreamy'], placing this show slightly behind 12/2/73 rather than above everything. The broad community weight, however, is strongly canonical.
listenFor: The Big River > Dark Star > Eyes of the World run is the centerpiece: one reviewer described the Dark Star as ranging "from cacophonous, to trippy, to happy and all points inbetween, right into a mesmerizing eyes" [source: 'runs the gambit from cacophonous, to trippy, to happy and all points inbetween, right into a mesmerizing eyes']. One listener singled out what makes this Eyes of the World special: "its structure is brilliant, Keith and Bob both play major roles, its tight and lose" and called the mix "perfect—perfect" [source: 'its structure is brilliant, Keith and Bob both play major roles, its tight and lose']. There is also a notable Mountain Jam tease at the top of Mississippi Half-Step worth catching — one reviewer heard it as "a glimpse into the epic cow palace allman brothers show" [source: 'a glimpse ito the epic cow palace allman brothers show (12/31/73)']. The recording itself draws praise: one listener noted it has "a very very good mix" with the drums not overpowering the rest of the band [source: 'this one has a very very good mix']. After the great second set run, one reviewer is direct that "the rest of the show is nothing special" past that peak [source: 'After that segment the rest of the show is nothing special'].
context: November 1973 sits squarely in the Wall of Sound era, when the Dead were running the massive PA system that defined their mid-'70s live sound. This recording comes from a soundboard source (identifier: gd73-11-11.sbd.schlissel.14105.sbeok.shnf) with brief audience patches covering dropout sections in Eyes of the World and Half-Step. The show was officially released as part of 'Winterland 1973: The Complete Recordings,' giving it the band organization's stamp of endorsement. One reviewer placed it alongside "the legendary Harper college show, the spring 77 shows, and the epic europe shows from 1972" as a must-have [source: 'this show is up there with the legendary Harper college show, the spring 77 shows, and the epic europe shows from 1972'].
funFact: One attendee recalled that after the encore, the crowd refused to leave for 25 solid minutes — clapping, screaming, and stomping in unison — until the house lights came back down and the band returned for a double encore [source: 'we set ourselves to stomping on the floor. Then we clapped, screamed "MORE" and stomped the floor simultaneously, in unison and as one unified body for 25 solid, nonstop minutes'].
headline: Dark Star into Eyes, Winterland, November '73.
